title: The Parable of Two Eagles and a Vine

questions.question: What riddle and parable does Ezekiel declare to the house of Israel?
options: A great eagle with great wings came to Lebanon and took the top of the cedar
A lion from the thicket devoured a sheep
A bear from the north destroyed a vineyard
A serpent bit the heel of a king
questions.correctAnswer: A great eagle with great wings came to Lebanon and took the top of the cedar
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:3 (ESV): "A great eagle with great wings and long pinions, rich in plumage of many colors, came to Lebanon and took the top of the cedar."

questions.question: Where did the eagle carry the topmost of the young twigs?
options: To a land of trade, and set it in a city of merchants
To the highest mountain peak in the world
To a desolate wilderness
To an island in the middle of the sea
questions.correctAnswer: To a land of trade, and set it in a city of merchants
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:4 (ESV): "He broke off the topmost of its young twigs and carried it to a land of trade and set it in a city of merchants."

questions.question: What did the eagle do with the seed of the land?
options: Planted it in fertile soil, placed it beside abundant waters like a willow twig
Cast it upon the rocks where it withered
Fed it to the birds of the air
Crushed it under its talons
questions.correctAnswer: Planted it in fertile soil, placed it beside abundant waters like a willow twig
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:5 (ESV): "Then he took of the seed of the land and planted it in fertile soil. He placed it beside abundant waters. He set it like a willow twig,"

questions.question: What did the seed become?
options: A low, spreading vine
A towering oak tree
A fruitful fig tree
A field of wheat
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:6 (ESV): "and it sprouted and became a low, spreading vine..."

questions.question: When another great eagle with great wings and much plumage appeared, what did the vine do?
options: It bent its roots toward him and shot forth its branches toward him, that he might water it
It shriveled up in fear
It wrapped its branches around the first eagle
It produced rotten grapes
questions.correctAnswer: It bent its roots toward him and shot forth its branches toward him, that he might water it
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:7 (ESV): "But there was another great eagle with great wings and much plumage, and behold, this vine bent its roots toward him and shot forth its branches toward him from the bed where it was planted, that he might water it."

questions.question: What is the question God asks about the vine bending toward the second eagle?
options: "Will it thrive? Will he not pull up its roots and cut off its fruit, so that it withers...?"
"Will it become a cedar?"
"Shall the eagles fight over it?"
"Will it produce wine for the king?"
questions.correctAnswer: "Will it thrive? Will he not pull up its roots and cut off its fruit, so that it withers...?"
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:9 (ESV): "Say, Thus says the Lord God: Will it thrive? Will he not pull up its roots and cut off its fruit, so that it withers, so that all its fresh sprouting leaves wither?"

questions.question: Who does the first great eagle represent in the explanation of the parable?
options: The king of Babylon
The king of Egypt
The Lord Himself
The prophet Ezekiel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:12 (ESV): "Say now to the rebellious house, Do you not know what these things mean? Tell them, behold, the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, and took her king and her princes and brought them to him to Babylon."

questions.question: What did the king of Babylon do with the seed of the land (the new king of Judah)?
options: Made a covenant with him and put him under oath
Killed him immediately
Blinded him and bound him in chains
Made him ruler over all Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: Made a covenant with him and put him under oath
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:13 (ESV): "And he took one of the royal offspring and made a covenant with him, putting him under oath (the chief men of the land he had taken away),"

questions.question: Why did the new king of Judah send ambassadors to Egypt (the second eagle)?
options: That they might give him horses and a large army
To buy grain during the famine
To find a wife for his son
To seek the wisdom of Pharaoh
questions.correctAnswer: That they might give him horses and a large army
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:15 (ESV): "But he rebelled against him by sending his ambassadors to Egypt, that they might give him horses and a large army."

questions.question: What does God ask concerning the king of Judah who broke the covenant?
options: "Will he thrive? Can one escape who does such things? Can he break the covenant and yet escape?"
"Will Pharaoh protect him?"
"Will the walls of Jerusalem hold?"
"Why did he not trust in his own strength?"
questions.correctAnswer: "Will he thrive? Can one escape who does such things? Can he break the covenant and yet escape?"
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:15 (ESV): "Will he thrive? Can one escape who does such things? Can he break the covenant and yet escape?"

questions.question: God says, "As I live, surely it is... that he despised, and... that he broke. I will return it upon his head."
options: My oath / my covenant
King Nebuchadnezzar's word / Babylon's law
The temple / the altar
The priests / the sabbath
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:19 (ESV): "Therefore thus says the Lord God: As I live, surely it is my oath that he despised, and my covenant that he broke. I will return it upon his head."

questions.question: Where will God bring the rebel king, to enter into judgment with him there?
options: Babylon
Egypt
Jerusalem
The wilderness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:20 (ESV): "I will spread my net over him, and he shall be taken in my snare, and I will bring him to Babylon and enter into judgment with him there for the treachery he has committed against me."

questions.question: In the messianic promise at the end of the chapter, what does the Lord God say He Himself will plant?
options: A sprig from the lofty top of the cedar
A mighty vineyard in the desert
A new temple of living stones
An olive tree bearing twelve fruits
questions.correctAnswer: A sprig from the lofty top of the cedar
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:22 (ESV): "Thus says the Lord God: I myself will take a sprig from the lofty top of the cedar and will set it out. I will break off from the topmost of its young twigs a tender one, and I myself will plant it on a high and lofty mountain."

questions.question: Where will the Lord plant this tender sprig?
options: On the mountain height of Israel
In the valley of dry bones
In the garden of Eden
Beside the river of life
questions.correctAnswer: On the mountain height of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:23 (ESV): "On the mountain height of Israel will I plant it, that it may bear branches and produce fruit and become a noble cedar."

questions.question: What will happen when the noble cedar grows?
options: And under it will dwell every kind of bird; in the shade of its branches birds of every sort will nest
It will touch the heavens and be seen by all nations
It will weep sap to heal the nations
It will bear fruit of gold and silver
questions.correctAnswer: And under it will dwell every kind of bird; in the shade of its branches birds of every sort will nest
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 17:23 (ESV): "And under it will dwell every kind of bird; in the shade of its branches birds of every sort will nest."

key_verse_text: "And all the trees of the field shall know that I am the Lord; I bring low the high tree, and make high the low tree, dry up the green tree, and make the dry tree flourish. I am the Lord; I have spoken, and I will do it."
